questions.question: The telephone was invented by:
questions.rationale: Bell's 1876 patent is the credited invention — Elisha Gray filed a rival caveat the same day, a footnote exams occasionally weaponise.

questions.question: The electron was discovered by:
questions.rationale: Thomson found the electron (1897), Rutherford the proton, Chadwick the neutron (1932) — the subatomic ladder that answers three questions in every paper.

questions.question: Penicillin was discovered by:
questions.rationale: Fleming noticed the mould's antibacterial effect in 1928; Florey and Chain developed it into medicine, and all three shared the 1945 Nobel.

questions.question: The World Wide Web was invented by:
questions.rationale: Berners-Lee proposed and built the Web at CERN in 1989 — distinct from the Internet's underlying protocols, which is the deeper version of the question.

questions.question: X-rays were discovered by:
questions.rationale: Röntgen's 1895 discovery earned the very first Physics Nobel (1901); Becquerel and the Curies followed with radioactivity.

questions.question: The periodic table's periodic law was formulated by:
questions.rationale: Mendeleev's 1869 table even predicted the properties of elements yet to be discovered — the exam's favourite embellishment.

questions.question: The Wright brothers are credited with:
options: The first powered, controlled airplane flight
questions.rationale: Kitty Hawk, 1903 — powered, controlled, sustained. The helicopter belongs to Sikorsky and the jet to Whittle and von Ohain.

questions.question: The Raman effect, announced in 1928, earned C.V. Raman the Nobel Prize in:
questions.rationale: The discovery was announced on 28 February 1928 (now National Science Day); the Physics Nobel followed in 1930 — two years apart, the fact the paper tests.

questions.question: The DNA double helix structure was worked out by:
questions.rationale: Watson and Crick published the structure in 1953, building on Rosalind Franklin's X-ray diffraction images — the trio fact the options quietly acknowledge.

questions.question: The concept of the zero's arithmetic rules was first formally set out by:
questions.rationale: Brahmagupta's Brahmasphutasiddhanta (628 CE) gives the earliest formal rules for zero's arithmetic; Aryabhata's system supplied the place-value foundation.
